title: Affine formal equivalence with quotient-system and section-limit natural comparisons
statement: Let X be an affine Noetherian scheme, J ideal sheaf data, and Coh(X,J) the coherent formal category [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put A=Gamma(X,top), I=J(top), S=AdicCompletion I A [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let F be the full category of finite S-modules, R:F to Mod_A scalar restriction, L=tilde followed by pullback along X.isoSpec [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and C=L followed by formalCompletionFunctor J. Let W send a formal system to its actual diagram of top section A-modules. There exist an equivalence E:F equivalent to Coh(X,J), a natural isomorphism beta:E.functor followed by the formal-system inclusion isomorphic to R followed by C, and a natural isomorphism gamma:R isomorphic to E.functor followed by the inclusion, W and categorical lim. Both comparisons apply to every finite S-module and every S-linear map. No presentation, chosen formal map, eta, torsion condition or annihilator estimate is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 087W, lemma-inverse-systems-affine, together with the canonical affine chart (01IB) and completion comparisons (00MA, 05GG)

proof.text: Put A=Gamma(X,top), I=J(top), e=X.isoSpec and K=J.comap e.inv. Cancel e.hom.appTop to prove e.inv.appTop=GammaSpecIso.inv, then use ext_of_isAffine and ideal_top_comap_of_isAffine to prove K=ofIdealTop (I.map GammaSpecIso.inv). Comap composition gives K.comap e.hom=J. The affine component is Noetherian by Mathlib IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian.

Apply exists_formalSystemsPullback in both directions to get P and Q together with equations for their underlying system functors. Whisker tensor-pullback composition and identity isomorphisms by the inverse-system functor. The equations for P and Q identify their underlying composites with the identity. Lift these isomorphisms through the fully faithful inclusions and form T=Equivalence.mk P Q. Apply coherentFormalModules_affine to A,I,K. Its inverse followed by T.inverse is the required E.

For a quasi-coherent sheaf, modulePullbackIdealPowerProductImage identifies the target power-product inclusion with the image of the pulled-back source inclusion. Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk, cokernel.mapIso, cokernelImageι and preservation of cokernels give the quotient isomorphism. Its composite with the quotient projection is the pulled-back projection. Precompose with the epimorphic quotient projection to prove compatibility both with lower powers and with sheaf maps. Assemble these as a natural completion/pullback comparison for H=R followed by tilde. Every tilde sheaf is quasi-coherent, even when the restricted completed module is not finite over A. Whisker the Spec inverse comparison by termwise tensor pullback, rewrite the inclusion equation for Q, and compose with this completion comparison. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensor pullback with Scheme.Modules.pullback and gives beta.

Pushforward along e.hom and e.inv gives an equivalence on module sheaves. Its adjunction and the tensor-pullback adjunction identify tensorPullback e.inv with pushforward e.hom. GammaSpecIso.inv followed by e.hom.appTop is the identity, so ModuleCat.restrictScalarsComp' identifies its Spec sections with actual top sections on X, naturally. Whisker by inverse systems and the formal inclusion; use the equation for P to obtain d:IX followed by W is isomorphic to P followed by IY and Spec section diagrams. Whisker d by Q and cancel Q followed by P using the already constructed ambient counit v. This gives dQ:Q followed by IX and W is isomorphic to IY followed by Spec section diagrams.

For each Spec formal module F, the supplied limiting cone gives a canonical isomorphism from the restricted E.functor(F) to the categorical limit of its Spec section diagram. These form a natural isomorphism: compose the naturality equation with each limit projection, rewrite limMap_pi and conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp, and apply the supplied cone naturality hn. Whisker by the inverse Spec equivalence, compose with its counit under R, and compose with the inverse of dQ after lim to obtain gamma. All constructions use unrestricted ideals and arbitrary affine schemes, including zero ideals, unit ideals and the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModules_affine_global_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) :
    let A := Γ(X, ⊤)
    let I := J.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩
    let S := AdicCompletion I A
    let F := ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun Q : ModuleCat.{u} S ↦ Module.Finite S Q)
    let R := ObjectProperty.ι (fun Q : ModuleCat.{u} S ↦ Module.Finite S Q) ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A S)
    let C := tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom ⋙
      formalCompletionFunctor J
    let W := (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ X.Modules (ModuleCat A)).obj
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤))
    ∃ E : F ≌ CoherentFormalModule X J,
      Nonempty (E.functor ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule J).ι ≅ R ⋙ C) ∧
      Nonempty (R ≅ E.functor ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule J).ι ⋙ W ⋙ lim)
